html:
Moshoeshoe I was the founder of the Basotho nation and of the kingdom that became Lesotho, ruling from the 1820s until his death in 1870.

In the wars and famines of the 1820s, when the rise of the Zulu state under Shaka sent refugees across the highveld, he gathered scattered groups on the mountain of Thaba Bosiu, offering land and cattle to those who joined him. He won by diplomacy as much as by war, sending cattle to enemies he had beaten.

He invited French missionaries to Morija in 1833. Pressed by the Boers of the Orange Free State in the Free State wars, he asked for British protection, which came in 1868 and kept Lesotho out of South Africa. His founding day is a national holiday.
sum: Moshoeshoe I was the founder of the Basotho nation and of the kingdom that became Lesotho, ruling from the 1820s until his death in 1870.
